record.name: El Salvador
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The 2025 AI promotion law created a National AI Agency that runs a registry and issues standards, but its own rules limit its checks to confirming that controls exist and leave impact assessments to registered operators.

related_bodies.name: Agencia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (ANIA)
related_bodies.role: It promotes AI and provides light-touch supervision through a registry, standards, a sandbox, and voluntary and mandatory registration; no mandate for it to evaluate advanced models was identified, so it is not counted.

record.notes: Borderline case, kept as none identified. The agency (ANIA, created by Legislative Decree 234 of 26 February 2025 and now a decentralised public body) has a division for technical standards, risk frameworks and safety criteria, a voluntary registry with legal safeguards, a mandatory registry for consequential decisions in health, finance, public biometrics and public services, and a supervised sandbox. Its Resolution 0001/2025 (primary, read in full as text) says compliance checks focus on confirming that controls exist 'rather than a detailed technical review' (Art. 17) and that algorithmic impact assessments are done by the operators (Art. 15). The resolution provides for no testing or evaluation of AI models by the agency. The law text itself (Decree 234) was not read; its description comes from the resolution and a press report. Resolution 0001/2025 Art. 19 prohibits requiring disclosure of source code, model architecture, weights or training data and bars mandatory third-party audits of these, and Art. 12(a) exempts providers of models, APIs and cloud services from mandatory registration on that basis alone; Art. 19 also limits ANIA to requesting high-level system descriptions, statistical summaries, performance metrics, dataset hashes and compliance statements. These limits concern what ANIA may require of providers; no mandate for ANIA to evaluate advanced models was identified. Legislative Decree 674 (Diario Oficial No. 178, 25 September 2026) sets special rules for carrying out national AI, robotics and similar technology projects; as read on 9 November 2026 it neither amends nor repeals Resolution 0001/2025.
